title: For the Love of the City Showcase adjusts on the fly for Saturday's big event, now at Fike - NewsBreak
text:
By Paul Durham ,
15 hours ago
As Jeremy Jeffers of Team Power Foundation and Rod Bridgers of The Hoop State Network were working to put together a historic day of high school hoops in Wilson with the inaugural For the Love of the City showcase, one obstacle they didn’t foresee was football.
When the NCHSAA football championship schedule was announced Friday evening with Hunt High playing Crest High of Shelby in 5-A final on Saturday night in Durham, the dominoes started to fall. Hunt was set to host the For the Love of the City Showcase featuring all eight high school boys basketball teams from Wilson in action but not with its football team playing for a state title. In fact, the Warriors opted to pull out of the showcase altogether in order for the players to attend the state championship game.
Some last-minute scrambling was necessary but Jeffers and Bridgers sorted out the details to keep the FLOC Showcase alive. Instead of Hunt hosting eight games on Saturday, Dec. 8, Fike High’s Harvey Reid Jr. Court will be the site of seven games, followed by a watch party with Hunt’s game against Crest broadcast on a big screen.
Fike will take Hunt’s place and face Farmville Central in the final game that starts at 6:30 p.m.
“Yeah, it’s been a crazy 48 hours for Rod and myself, but we’ve adjusted, and we were able to get it done and still try to bring this community event,” Jeffers said in a Tuesday morning telephone interview. “We’re super happy for the Hunt football team, and we’re actually doing a watch party instead of the 8 o’clock game, Hunt-Farmville Central, we moved everything up. And we’re doing a watch party at the Fike gymnasium, because we move everything to Fike, so we’re doing a free community watch party for people to come out and support the football team, so we decided to do that as well to show our support to the community.”
The day’s action begins at 11 a.m. with Sallie B. Howard School and Wilson Christian squaring off for the first time. Next up at 12:30 p.m. is Beddingfield facing St. Christopher Academy, an independent private school in Wake Forest, followed by Community Christian versus Faith Christian of Rocky Mount at 2 p.m.
Wilson Prep meets fellow NCHSAA 1-A contender Southern Wake Academy at 3:30 p.m. while Greenfield matches up with NCHSAA 6-A Southern Durham at 5 p.m.
Fike’s gym will also be the site, once again, of the For the Love of the City alumni games, featuring four games Sunday, Dec. 14, involving former high school hoopsters from the early 2000s through the last decade. The FLOC alumni games were started several years ago by Jeffers and Team Power Foundation co-founder and former teammate at Greenfield School, Darian CaHill, as a way to not only bring the community together but to do it for a great cause. All proceeds from the two days of games will go to making some needy families’ Christmas a lot better.
“Yeah, I think the biggest thing was getting all the coaches on board to understand the cause of the event,” Jeffers said. “And I think once they understood the cause, it was really a no-brainer for a lot of the coaches. Obviously, we’re raising money for families in Wilson for Christmas. And I think, you know, the cause really, really, really helped focus the coaches in on the bigger goal and the bigger Wilson, and us coming together instead of being divided and the kids as well.”
The FLOC alumni games will start at 3 p.m. and continue each hour on the hour Sunday. The full schedule and rosters for alumni games is listed below.
Jeffers said that the high school showcase on Saturday will also be a chance for local players to be seen by college recruiters.
“There will be some college coaches in attendance at certain games this weekend,” he said. “It brings an opportunity for our kids to be able to be seen that they may not have throughout the season. So the best of both worlds of giving back to our community and showcasing kids on a platform that may help them get recruited is what it’s all about.”
Truthfully, the sense of community is what made the first For the Love of the City alumni games in 2018 an instant hit. Old high school rivalries were re-ignited but in a warm, fuzzy way. Bringing in current high school players just adds to the layers of a true hometown classic that breathes the spirit of the season into the gathering.
“It makes us feel amazing that is a part of the of the brand of For the Love of the City,” Jeffers said. “It’s really for the love of everybody. When we did the media day with the kids, it just gave me chills to see all those schools, and kids from each school and under one roof. To get them to play against outside schools—other than the Sallie B. Howard-Wilson Christian game—is going to be a sense of Wilson versus everybody at the event. So, that sense of community, of everybody’s cheering for the Wilson team will be special, man, and I’m excited for Saturday!”
